subject: Spend-smoothing proposal and burst protection (credits escrow option)
messages:
From: Monica Ruiz <monica.ruiz@aurumhealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing clarification: minimum spend smoothing & burst protection

Diego —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to get clarity on how Redwood handles month-to-month variability. Our usage forecast is lumpy (big batches at month end). Two items we need clarified before legal will proceed:  

1) Minimum spend / commit: we are comfortable with a soft monthly commit but need an option to carry unused committed credits forward (smoothing) so we don't overpay for quiet months. Can Redwood provide a formal mechanism for rolling credits or a monthly true-up that smooths over a quarter?

2) Burst/on-demand over-commit: when we spike above commit, what on-demand premium applies? We want a cap on the effective premium during sustained spikes (e.g., if we exceed commit by >50% for a week).

Also, procurement asked whether Redwood will accept an escrowed deposit model (prepaid credits held in escrow, released weekly as consumed) as an alternative to a hard multi-month commit. If you can send a short proposal with a few options and an example math for our forecast (attached), that will help move this to legal.

Thanks,
Monica Ruiz
Head of Procurement — Aurum Health

Attachments: Aurum-usage-forecast.xlsx (xlsx)

From: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Pricing clarification: minimum spend smoothing & burst protection

Team — forwarding Aurum's ask (see attached forecast). Short timeline: they want options to present to legal this week. High level asks: smoothing mechanism for soft commit, capped premium for on-demand bursts, and whether escrowed prepaid credits are acceptable.

Quick thoughts: I think a 'quarterly smoothing buffer' + a capped burst premium is the cleanest for us (keeps revenue predictable, lower legal friction). Escrowed credits are workable but we need to define reconciliation cadence and early refund rules.

Can you please draft three options with recommended contract language and sample math for their forecast? I'm thinking: Option 1 — Soft monthly commit with 3-month rolling buffer (unused credits carry forward within the quarter) + 30% on-demand premium up to a 2x cap per day; Option 2 — Fixed monthly floor (60% of forecast) with 20% on-demand premium and a monthly true-up; Option 3 — Prepaid escrow credits (90-day escrow, weekly release) with lower per-token rates but non-refundable after 30 days.

Attach draft term sheet and I'll share back.

- Diego

Diego / team —

I've sketched the three options and attached a short term-sheet plus worked examples against Aurum's forecast. Highlights below; numbers are illustrative for negotiation (we can toggle):

Option A — Quarterly smoothing buffer (recommended)- Commitment: monthly nominal commit equal to forecasted month- Carry-forward: unused monthly credits roll into a 3-month rolling buffer (unused credits expire after quarter)- On-demand: +30% premium per-token over commit price; daily spike cap: 2x on-demand rate for sustained spikes (>48 hours); quarterly true-up reconciles net consumption vs committed spend- Example: forecast month 1 = 10M tokens at $0.0035/token commit price; if month usage = 16M tokens, 6M billed at on-demand price $0.0035*1.3 = $0.00455 (capped if sustained)

Option B — Monthly floor + monthly true-up- Floor: 60% of forecast billed at discounted commit price- On-demand: +20% premium over commit price for consumption above floor- True-up: monthly invoicing adjusts next month; unused credit refundable quarterly (less admin fee)

Option C — Escrowed prepaid credits- Prepay: customer deposits funds to escrow for 90 days; credits released weekly as consumed- Pricing: lower per-token rate (e.g., $0.0032/token) in exchange for 90-day escrow lock and 30-day non-refundable window- Reconciliation: unused funds refundable at 90-day mark minus reconciliation adjustment

Recommended approach: Option A. It addresses procurement's carry-forward ask and protects Redwood revenue by limiting arbitrage with the 3-month expiry and capped sustained-spike premium. It also minimizes accounting churn vs escrow.

I've attached the term sheet text for review — please add legal phrasing if you need hard commit language.

- Rachel

Attachments: Redwood-spend-smoothing-term-sheet-v1.pdf (pdf)

From: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Spend-smoothing proposal and draft term-sheet (three options)

Monica —

Thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the forecast. We've put together three practical options; attached is a short term-sheet plus worked examples mapped to your numbers. Summary:

- We recommend Option A (Quarterly smoothing buffer) — it gives you the carry-forward behavior procurement asked for while keeping billing reconciliation simple. Unused credits roll within the quarter, then expire.
- On-demand spike handling: a nominal premium over the commit price (30% in Option A) with a sustained-spike cap to avoid runaway daily premiums. For short spikes you pay the premium; for sustained usage we apply a cap to the effective daily rate to avoid bill shock while preserving unit economics.
- Escrowed prepaid credits (Option C) is acceptable if Aurum prefers that model; pricing improves modestly in exchange for escrow and longer lock window. We'll require a reconciliation cadence and a simple refund schedule (90-day window, 30-day non-refundable portion) to avoid revenue leakage.

Please see the attached examples; if Option A looks good, I've proposed the following contract language to insert into the MSA: 

"Spend smoothing: Customer's monthly committed credits may be carried forward into a rolling three-month buffer. Unused credits remaining at the end of the rolling period expire. On-demand usage above committed credits is billed at the on-demand premium, subject to a sustained spike cap defined as the maximum effective daily rate applied when overages persist longer than 48 hours."

If you'd like, we can convert Option A into redline-ready language for your legal team. Any preference or tweaks?

Regards,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Monica Ruiz <monica.ruiz@aurumhealth.com>

Diego / Rachel —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Option A aligns with our procurement goals. A few small asks before we loop legal:  

1) Can the sustained-spike cap be defined as a 1.6x cap (vs 2x) for the first occurrence per quarter? That gives us breathing room for a single unexpected push without a massive premium.
2) For the carry-forward window: can we allow a one-time per-year extension of 30 days in writing (to cover business seasonality)?

If you can confirm those two items in the term sheet, we'll send to our legal team next week. Otherwise this is good to go.

Thanks,
Monica Ruiz
Head of Procurement — Aurum Health
